children: From a valuation perspective,
Village Super Market, Inc.

VLGEA stock looks attractive. VLGEA is currently trading at a trailing 12-month enterprise value/sales (EV/sales) of 0.24X, a roughly 79% discount compared with the industry average of 1.16X. VLGEA also trades at a lower valuation compared to other industry players, such as
J Sainsbury plc
JSAIY and
Tesco PLC
TSCDY. Currently, JSAIY and TSCDY have EV/sales multiples of 0.23X and 0.44X, respectively.

Though VLGEA’s cheap valuation may present a potentially profitable opportunity for investors seeking value, a more comprehensive analysis is needed to determine if its discounted valuation is justified based on its fundamentals and growth prospects.
VLGEA Stock’s Price Performance

VLGEA’s shares have gained 16.5% in the past year compared with the industry’s 3.8% growth. It has also outperformed J Sainsbury and Tesco, which have rallied 1.1% and 9.2%, respectively, in the same time frame.
Business Tailwinds for VLGEA

Village’s ongoing store investment program remains a key growth driver. The East Orange replacement ShopRite opened on May 27, 2026, while a Galloway replacement store is expected to open in fiscal 2027. Management also plans smaller remodels, merchandising projects and technology and equipment upgrades. These investments can expand selling capacity, refresh the customer experience and support sales growth while strengthening its regional store network.

Village continues to benefit from growth in digital sales, recently replaced or remodeled stores, fresh departments and pharmacy sales. Excluding the impact of Winter Storm Fern, third-quarter same-store sales rose 1.3%, while same-store sales increased 2.4% over the first 39 weeks of fiscal 2026. Management expects fiscal 2026 same-store sales growth of 1.5% to 2.5%, indicating that these operating initiatives should continue supporting underlying revenue momentum through year-end.

Village’s financial flexibility is supported by stronger operating cash flow and ample borrowing capacity. Net cash from operating activities rose to $78.5 million in the first 39 weeks of fiscal 2026 from $71.6 million a year earlier, while working capital improved to $30.1 million. The company also had nearly $66 million available under its revolving credit line as of April 25, 2026. In September 2026, the board declared quarterly cash dividend of 25 cents per share.

Village benefits from its Wakefern membership, which provides purchasing, distribution, technology, marketing and advertising scale typically associated with larger chains. The company also offers online ordering across its ShopRite, Fairway and Gourmet Garage banners, supported by loyalty programs and digital coupons. Combined with broad fresh-food offerings and larger store formats, these capabilities can strengthen customer engagement and help Village compete across both physical and digital grocery channels.
Headwinds for VLGEA’s Business

Village faces pressure from a highly competitive, low-margin grocery environment. Lower Wakefern patronage dividends and rebates, higher warehouse assessments, unfavorable product mix and increased promotional spending weighed on profitability, while utility, repair, insurance, employee and professional-service costs added expense pressure. The company also remains heavily dependent on Wakefern for merchandise and support services, while geographic concentration, unionized labor exposure and ongoing litigation with Wakefern add further risk.
Conclusion

Overall, Village’s store investments, digital growth, operating momentum and financial flexibility support its growth prospects, while margin pressures, rising costs, competitive intensity and Wakefern-related dependence are likely to put pressure on performance.
VLGEA’s undervaluation, despite the rise in share price, presents a lucrative opportunity for investors to add the stock to their portfolio.
